title: Junior Scientist Conference Grants
amount_raw: Grants up to £200 … (A); Grants of up to £500 … (B); up to £750 (Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored); Grants of up to £300 … (C)
eligibility_summary: Genetics Society 'junior scientist' members. Scheme A: undergraduate, Master's and PhD student members and postdoctoral members within six years of PhD viva. Schemes B and C: PhD student and postdoctoral members within six years of viva only. B and C require a UK base for conferences outside the UK, or a non-UK base for a UK conference. Applicants must present a poster or give a talk; the supervisor's supporting letter must come from a current Society member.
summary: Conference support in three streams: (A) up to £200 travel and accommodation for Genetics Society or Special Interest Group meetings, (B) up to £500 for non-Society genetics conferences (up to £750 for two Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored awards a year, PhD students only), and (C) up to £300 registration for virtual conferences.
notes: Open on the snapshot date: the page sets recurring bi-monthly deadlines, 'the 1st day of February, April, June, August, October and December'. The two deadlines recorded are the next two falling after 2026-08-28 (the 1 August 2026 round had already passed); the cycle repeats indefinitely, hence multi_deadline. Streams A/B/C are documented as 'three main streams' of a single named grant with one application route in the mySociety portal, so they are ONE row per the one-row-per-scheme rule; amount_min/max span the streams (£200 floor for stream A, £750 ceiling for the Adelphi co-sponsored award).

title: Training Grant
eligibility_summary: All Genetics Society members studying or working in the UK, or attending a course held in the UK. Students may apply as soon as they become members; other applicants must have been members for at least one year. A student's supervisor must also be a Society member and supply a supporting letter. One travel grant per member in any two-year period and one funded application per research group in any twelve-month period.
summary: Grants of up to £1,200 for members to attend formal short training courses, or to make a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic or genomic techniques; covers travel, accommodation, subsistence and registration/tuition fees.
notes: Open on the snapshot date: 'Deadlines for this grant are quarterly, at midnight on 15th February, May, August and November.' The 15 August 2026 round closed 13 days before the snapshot, so the two dates recorded are the next two in the cycle (2026-11-15 and 2027-02-15). Fieldwork is explicitly redirected to the Heredity Fieldwork Grant, confirming these are distinct schemes.

title: Public Engagement
eligibility_summary: Members of the Genetics Society. Excludes salaries, freelance fees, insurance, institutional overheads, room hire inside academic institutions, engagement that should have been costed into a UKRI or charity-funded grant, research data collection, for-profit media, and attendee travel. Travel must be economy class and UK-based.
summary: Grants of up to £1,000 for public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually, covering eligible travel and materials costs; successful applicants must acknowledge the Society, use its logo, follow the EDI principles and report participation numbers.
notes: Open on the snapshot date: 'The Public Engagement Grant has two deadlines per year (1st March and 1st October).' The 1 March 2026 round had passed, so the recorded dates are the next two in the cycle. Note the mirror-relative path preserves the site's own misspelling of the slug ('public-engement-grant').

title: One-off Meeting
amount_raw: The major sponsorship levels for the last 12 months have been between £1,000 and £2,000
eligibility_summary: Genetics Society members organising a genetics-themed meeting not run by the Society. Meetings must be based in, or have strong links with, the UK. Grants are for organising a meeting, not attending one, and the budget must include a Carer's Award allowance.
summary: Sponsorship of one-off genetics-themed meetings organised outside the Society, at several levels — a few hundred pounds for a named Genetics Society lecture, up to about £1,000 for a Society session, and potentially several thousand as major sponsor of an entire meeting.
notes: Rolling per the protocol: 'Members may apply at any time of the year', with review at the end of each month and a four-to-six-week response, so there is no fixed deadline and the page presents the call as continuously open. Amounts are marked uncertain because the page gives a band for recent awards (£1,000-£2,000) alongside 'potentially several thousand pounds' with no stated ceiling; the recorded min/max are the stated recent band, not a hard limit. FLAG FOR REVIEW: the page carries a standing caveat, 'we are currently reviewing our guidelines for grant applications and therefore the details below are subject to change in the near future'.

title: SIG
eligibility_summary: Genetics research communities wishing to run a regular series of meetings; open to undergraduates, graduate students, junior postdocs and PIs/Co-Is per the eligibility table. Meetings must be based in, or have strong links with, the UK. Applications must be submitted at least three months before the first meeting.
summary: Special Interest Group funding of up to £2,000 a year to sponsor a regular series of themed genetics research meetings; current groups include Seed Plant, e-ACGT, the C. elegans Group and the London Genetics Network.
notes: Rolling per the protocol: no deadline is stated, applications are simply due at least three months before the first meeting and the Society 'aims to respond to applications within four weeks'. Title is recorded verbatim from the page heading, 'SIG' (the body text calls it 'Special Interest Group Funding' and the eligibility table calls it 'New Special Interest Group') — title marked uncertain because the three names disagree; the canonical page slug is /new-special-interest-group/.

title: Carer’s Award
eligibility_summary: Any Genetics Society member with caring responsibilities, regardless of the age of the person they care for; priority is given to early-career scientists and according to need. Awards must be applied for before the meeting or event and are competitive.
summary: Award of up to £60 a day to support a member's attendance at a Genetics Society meeting or event where caring responsibilities would otherwise prevent it; claimable in arrears on production of electronic receipts.
notes: Rolling: no deadline is given anywhere; the award is tied to individual events ('Awards must be applied for prior to the meeting or event') and is also offered as an add-on within the Summer Studentship, Research Access Placement and Communicating Your Science schemes. Status marked uncertain because the page never states in so many words that the call is currently open — it is inferred from the standing, event-linked application route. Tagged restricted: the number of awards is capped by anticipated event attendance. The £60 is a daily rate, not a total, so amount_max_gbp records the rate.

title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant
eligibility_summary: All Genetics Society members studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students may apply on joining; others must have been members for at least a year. The supervisor must also be a member. One funded application per research group per twelve months and one grant per member in any two-year period.
summary: Awards of up to £2,000, funded from income from the Society's journal Heredity, covering travel and accommodation costs for a field-based genetic research project whose results would suit publication in Heredity.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the only deadline the page states, 'The deadline for the next round is 1st February 2024', precedes the 2026-08-28 snapshot date by more than two years, so the page does not show a call accepting applications and states no future opening date.
notes: FLAG FOR REVIEW — this is the weakest exclusion in this funder's set. The page is otherwise fully live (detailed FAQ, active 'Applications are made online via the Genetics Society Grants application site' route, and the Training Grant page redirects fieldwork applicants here), which suggests the scheme is running and the '1st February 2024' line is simply a stale, unmaintained date rather than a genuine closure. Excluded because the protocol labels from what the page says, and the page's only date is two years past; status and deadlines are marked uncertain to record that. A human pass may well flip this to rolling/in-scope.

title: Summer Studentship
amount_raw: £425/week allowance for up to 8 weeks; Up to £750 to cover host laboratory expenses
eligibility_summary: Undergraduate students except those in their first or final year, normally in the summer of year 2 (or year 3 of a four-year degree); the project must be based at a UK university. Both the student and the host research group leader must be Genetics Society members. One application per student and per lab group. Cannot part-fund a larger project, extend an honours project, or fund an early PhD start.
summary: Summer research studentship paying £425 a week for up to eight weeks plus up to £750 of host-laboratory expenses, a funded place at the residential Summer School Workshop (University of Oxford, 2-4 September) and a Carer's Award where needed.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states 'The deadline for 2026 applications is 31st March 2026', which precedes the 2026-08-28 snapshot date, so the round was not accepting applications; no future opening date is given.
notes: Closed distractor, and a likely agent false positive: the page reads as fully active and its workshop date (2-4 September) is still in the future at the snapshot date, but that is the date awardees attend, not an application date. The grants hub carousel advertises this scheme under a sponsor name, 'Genes & Development Summer Studentship'; no separate page exists for that name, so it is treated as the same scheme rather than a second row. Success rate stated as around 25% in 2024.

title: Research Access Placements
amount_raw: Paid Summer studentship: £425/week for up to 8 weeks; Flexible allowance of £160 (e.g., travel); Up to £750 to cover research costs
eligibility_summary: Undergraduate students from underrepresented and/or minoritised backgrounds — including members of a minoritised group, those receiving the full student loan, those with a declared disability, refugee status or caring responsibilities. Students choose from a list of 49 projects in the application form.
summary: Fully paid summer research internships run with the BBSRC for undergraduates from underrepresented backgrounds: £425 a week for up to 8 weeks, a £160 flexible allowance, up to £750 of research costs, online workshops, an expenses-paid three-day residential workshop in Oxford, a year's Society membership and mentorship.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states 'Applications will open on Tuesday, 27th January and close on 31st March', a window that had closed by the 2026-08-28 snapshot date; no future opening date is given.
notes: Closed distractor. FLAG: the open/close sentence gives no YEAR ('Tuesday, 27th January … 31st March'); it is read as 2026 because the same page fixes the residential workshop at September 2026 and requires projects to conclude before 2 September 2026. Dates are therefore marked uncertain. Distinct from the Summer Studentship (separate page, separate eligibility row in the eligibility table, BBSRC co-funded), so labelled as its own candidate.

title: Communicating Your Science Workshop
amount_raw: each place on this workshop represents an investment of around £2000 by the society
eligibility_summary: PhD student and postdoctoral researcher members of the Society working in genetics and related areas (the eligibility table excludes undergraduates and PIs/Co-Is). Applications must be signed off by a supervisor who is a Genetics Society member.
summary: Funded place on a three-day residential science-communication workshop at Chicheley Hall, with tutoring in storytelling, public talks, hands-on demonstrations and multimedia; the Society covers UK travel, accommodation and meals for successful applicants.
exclusion_reason: Failed the inclusion rule: the page states 'The application deadline for the workshop is the 15th of February 2026' and that the workshop itself ran on 15th-17th April 2026 — both before the 2026-08-28 snapshot date — and it states no future opening date.
notes: Closed distractor. The benefit is a funded place rather than a cash award, so the numeric amount fields are blank and marked uncertain, with the Society's stated per-place cost (~£2,000) recorded verbatim in amount_raw. A Carer's Award of up to £60/day is offered alongside it; that is labelled separately as genetics-society-carers-award.
